title: Exact Inheritance of Confirmed A and Search for Confirmed B

lineage.predecessor_transport_rule: the carrier may vary, but the supplied git bundle must hash-match the frozen predecessor manifest and must materialize the exact inherited A commit

worker.identity_attestation: self-declared; not independently verified by runtime
worker.delegation_rule: mechanical browser transport is permitted; research reasoning, candidate selection, hyperparameter choice, train.py authorship, and scientific judgment may not be delegated to another model or subagent
worker.external_patch_rule: no external leaderboard, known-winning autoresearch patch, operator-supplied candidate idea, TOE conditioning, or post-outcome tuning may be introduced after preregistration

question: Starting from the exact confirmed A accepted in AUTORESEARCH-LIVE-003, can the same preregistered researcher produce a second train.py candidate B that clears the same receiver-owned objective twice before promotion?
invariant: exact inherited accepted state A precedes all B-search work; researcher proposal authority != receiver measurement authority != promotion authority

measurement.upstream_seed_policy: unchanged upstream fixed seeds: torch.manual_seed(42) and torch.cuda.manual_seed(42)
measurement.confirmation_semantics: fresh receiver invocation and fresh candidate training measurement from the same still-unpromoted inherited-A accepted base, using the identical candidate commit and same fixed-seed protocol

total_budget.note: At $1.60/hour the 150-minute wall ceiling is $4.00. Do not add funding or exceed the spend ceiling without ending this preregistered experiment and defining a successor.

claim_boundary: A positive result earns exact accepted-state inheritance of A followed by a separately confirmed and promoted B under the receiver boundary.
A positive result establishes cumulative governed optimization: accepted state advanced from confirmed A to separately confirmed B.
A positive result does not by itself establish recursive improvement because A changed the training system being optimized, not the process that generates subsequent improvements.
A failed B confirmation is preserved and the search stops; another apparent B is not sought in this experiment.
The worker identity and no-subagent rule are procedural, not cryptographically attested.
The experiment does not claim hostile-process or OS-level isolation.
Because upstream seed 42 remains fixed, confirmation is an operational repeat under the same fixed-seed protocol, not an independent-seed statistical replication.
Recursive-improvement language remains unearned unless a later experiment changes and validates the improvement-generating process itself.
